people.name: Adham Bedir
people.title: CEO
owns: Adham owns the customers, the contracts, the prices, and every conversation with the client.
He sets the direction of the company and the monthly targets. He makes the final decision on priorities.
He owns fundraising, the investors, and the company in the United States.
He owns the weekly update to the client and the month-end review.
people.whereWhen: He works from the United States, remotely. He comes to Egypt for launches and for big partnerships.
contactFor: Any problem that Moharam, Mano, or Ahmed Alaa cannot solve
Questions about the client
Strategy, new markets, and new customers
people.note: Moharam, Mano, and Ahmed Alaa contact Adham directly. Everyone else goes through their Portfolio Manager.

people.name: Youssif Siessa
people.title: CTO
owns: Youssif owns the technology: the dashboard, the tools, the integrations, and the AI products we will build in the future.
Quality is his area. The QC team reports to him through the Quality Control Lead.
He makes the technical decisions about the collection app, the exports, and how we handle data.
people.whereWhen: He works from the United States, remotely. He talks with Youssef Medhat every day about quality.
contactFor: A bug in a tool or in the dashboard, or a request for a new feature
How the collection app works
How the quality process is designed
people.escalateTo: Adham, for anything about customers, contracts, or prices.
people.note: He joins conversations with the client when the topic is technical.

people.name: Aly Siessa
people.title: CPO
owns: Aly owns everything a worker wears on the head: the rigs, the mounts, the caps, and the devices. He also owns the next generation of collection hardware.
He owns hardware design in Egypt and hardware procurement in China.
He sets the hardware standards: the camera angle, comfort, how long the hardware lasts, and safety on site.
people.whereWhen: He works from the United States, remotely. He reviews designs with Ali Ateem once a week.
contactFor: A fault in a rig or a mount that keeps coming back
A new kind of workplace that needs new hardware
Buying devices in large numbers
people.note: Ali Ateem does the everyday hardware fixes. Mano handles orders and replacements.

people.name: Moharam
people.title: Director of Operations
owns: Moharam owns field operations: every live site, every shift, and every daily target.
He manages the Portfolio Managers: their portfolios, their standards, and their launches.
He owns the operator bench. He hires through Mano, he trains the operators, and he decides which operators go to which site.
He checks and approves every new site launch.
He handles absences, incidents, device shortages, and the footage that is waiting to be uploaded each day.
He handles the day-to-day relationship with the site partners.
people.whereWhen: He is in the field every day, moving between sites. He meets Adham and Mano every day.
contactFor: Any problem on site that a Portfolio Manager cannot solve
An absence, if the Portfolio Manager has not answered within 20 minutes
An injury or an incident. Tell him within 30 minutes.
A site that is below target, phones that go offline, or footage that is building up and not uploaded
people.escalateTo: Adham, for planning, resources, problems with partners, and any emergency, at any hour of the day or night.
people.note: Moharam is responsible for everything that breaks in the field.

people.name: Mano
people.title: Chief of Staff
owns: Mano owns people: recruiting, offer letters, onboarding paperwork, the employee handbook, and this map.
He does the legal filings with the company lawyer: the tax card, ITIDA, data protection, and social insurance.
He orders gear and replaces gear. He arranges transport, storage, internet lines, and upload hubs.
He collects every Portfolio Manager's daily report and puts them together into one report for the whole company.
He keeps the target list of new sites and makes the first contact with them.
people.whereWhen: He is in Cairo, in the office and remote. He meets Adham and Moharam every day.
contactFor: Ordering or replacing gear
Hiring, onboarding documents, and ID and consent forms
Sending in or fixing a daily report
A new business or site to add to the target list
people.note: Everyone joins the company through Mano.

people.name: Ahmed Alaa
people.title: Head of Finance
owns: Ahmed Alaa owns payroll, payments to sites and workers, payments to partners, expense refunds, bonuses, and referral rewards.
He owns the monthly numbers: the invoice, the final total after the audit, and the money we owe to every site and partner.
He runs the month-end close: the audit with Youssef Medhat, the invoice, and payroll.
He gets a second approval from Adham for payments above the threshold.
people.whereWhen: He is in Cairo. He makes payments once a month. He sends the invoice after the audit.
contactFor: Salary, payments, expense refunds, bonuses, and referral rewards
An invoice or a partner statement
people.note: Payments above the approval threshold need a second approval from Adham.

people.name: HR
people.title: Hiring, paperwork, and the handbook
owns: HR recruits operators and staff. HR writes the offer letters, the contracts, and the onboarding paperwork.
HR keeps the employee handbook and this map.
HR arranges housing for workers who come from other cities.
HR keeps the gate papers for every wearer: a copy of the ID, the signed consent, the signed fraud briefing, and one account in their own name.
people.whereWhen: In Cairo, under Mano.
contactFor: Hiring, onboarding documents, and ID and consent forms
Contracts, offer letters, and questions about the handbook
Housing
people.note: Mano does this work until someone is hired for the seat.

people.name: Business development
people.title: Finding sites, the target list
owns: Business development keeps the target list of new sites. The list is ranked by the task categories we need and by the upload path.
It contacts new sites through people we know, and it also contacts sites directly.
It runs the referral program: 10% for a site contract that is signed.
It books meetings and hands them to Adham and Youssif. They close the deal.
people.whereWhen: In Cairo, and wherever the next site is.
contactFor: A business we should film in
A possible new site that a Portfolio Manager or an operator heard about
The target list
people.note: Mano does this work until someone is hired for the seat. The founders close every partnership.

people.name: Mazen
people.title: Head of Deployment
owns: Mazen owns a portfolio of sites and its monthly hour target.

He runs Day 0 at every new site, together with the site's Portfolio Manager. On Day 0 they set up the charging stations, label the hardware, check the network, show the operators the job, and make the pilot recordings.
He owns training: the first-day lessons for operators and Portfolio Managers.
He owns procurement: phones, mounts, caps, chargers, and spares. He orders them through Mano.
people.whereWhen: He is at new sites during launch weeks. The rest of the time he is at his own sites.
contactFor: Opening a new site and Day 0
Training for a new hire or a new site
Gear orders and how much stock we have
people.escalateTo: Moharam, for operations. Ahmed Alaa, for money.

people.name: Eyad
people.title: Portfolio Manager
owns: Eyad owns a portfolio of sites and a monthly hour target.
He runs the site team, which is the operators. Mano hires them, and Moharam assigns them to the site.
He runs the daily rotations, the 30-minute recording cycle, the restarts, the charging, and device custody.
He answers every quality flag within 24 hours. He gives the correction to the worker the same day.
He handles absences, people who do not show up, and the first response to any problem on the floor.
He sends the daily wrap report to Mano. The report has the hours, the active phones, the state of the hardware, the problems, and the fixes.
He looks for new sites for the portfolio.
people.whereWhen: He is on site every day, across his portfolio. He clocks in with the operators. He clocks out after the gear is returned and checked.
contactFor: The first person to contact, for every operator and wearer on his sites
Absence notices. Send them by 8 PM the night before.
Device and gear problems
Anything an operator cannot solve
people.escalateTo: Moharam, for operations. Mano, for money, gear, and procurement. Youssef Medhat, for quality.

people.name: Operators
people.title: One operator for every ten phones, under every Portfolio Manager
owns: There is one operator for every ten phones. Operators hand out the devices, fit the rigs, and check the camera angle. They run the 30-minute restarts and do the check at every reset. They watch the storage and the battery. At the end of the shift they collect the devices and put them on the dock.
They clock in and clock out every day. They hand the gear over to the Portfolio Manager every day.
people.whereWhen: They are on the floor for the whole shift, at the site they are assigned to.
contactFor: Wearers with a device problem talk to their operator first
people.note: Operators are KMSC staff. Wearers are the people who film. A wearer is an employee of the site, or a worker that KMSC recruited. Both operators and wearers pass onboarding screening.

people.name: Youssef Medhat
people.title: Quality Control Lead
owns: Youssef Medhat reviews every uploaded video. He keeps it, flags it, or deletes it.
He runs the daily audit. The audit checks the angle, the lighting, the movement, and the fraud patterns.
He sends flags to the Portfolio Managers the same day. He keeps the watchlist of workers who get repeated flags.
He owns the four-step QC process and the month-end audit.
He does the central planning: the dashboard, the dispatch schedule, and the order to procurement for every new site.
people.whereWhen: He is in Cairo, every day. He sends flags out the same day.
contactFor: What counts as fraud
A flag you disagree with, or a flag you want explained
The standards for angle, lighting, and framing
Questions about one recording session
The dispatch schedule: when phones and people move to a site
people.note: Portfolio Managers answer every flag within 24 hours.

people.name: QC reviewers
people.title: Quality Control team
owns: The reviewers review every video on the account. The size of the team depends on how many videos come in that month.
Mano hires the reviewers.
people.whereWhen: They work remotely, every day.
contactFor: Through Youssef Medhat

people.name: Ali Ateem
people.title: Hardware Design Engineer
owns: Ali Ateem designs the rigs and the mounts, and he improves them step by step.
He finds the cause of hardware failures that keep happening, and he fixes the cause.
He designs new mounts for new kinds of workplaces.
people.whereWhen: He is in Cairo. He designs with Aly. He gets parts through Mano.
contactFor: A rig problem that keeps happening across many phones
A site that needs a different mount

people.name: Open seat
people.title: Procurement, China
owns: This seat will buy devices and collection hardware in large numbers.
This seat will manage the suppliers and how long orders take to arrive.
people.whereWhen: In China, after we hire someone.
contactFor: Through Aly, until the seat is filled

people.name: Open seats
people.title: Tech team
owns: The tech team will build the software tools and the dashboard, connect the hardware to the software, and give technical support.
people.whereWhen: Planned. The team will be in Egypt.
contactFor: Through Youssif, until the seats are filled

people.name: Delivery partners
people.title: Partners outside the company
owns: Delivery partners are independent. They find their own sites, staff them, and deliver hours under their own agreement.
They follow every KMSC standard: onboarding screening, one account per person, and the quality rules.
people.whereWhen: At their own sites.
contactFor: Working together on operations, through Moharam
Payments, through Mano
people.escalateTo: Moharam, for operations. Mano, for money.
people.note: Partners are outside the org chart. Their people are not KMSC staff.
